newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan shows interest in long-term bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan shows interest in long-term bond issue.

text.p: Pakistan hopes to issue long-term foreign bonds as part of a strategy to reduce reliance on short-term borrowing, a senior official said on Thursday.
Moeen Afzal, Secretary at the Finance Ministry, said the caretaker government was examining a range of possible issues, but the choice and timing would depend on market conditions.
"We are looking at various options, and samurai bonds is one of the areas we are examining," he told Reuters, but gave no details.
The English-language daily Dawn quoted government officials on Thursday as saying Pakistan might float $350 million of samurai bonds to improve its balance of payments position.

A banking source said Finance Ministry officials met foreign bankers on Thursday to hear their proposals for raising short- and medium-term money for the government. The outcome of the meetings was not immediately known.

President Farooq Leghari installed a caretaker government with a 90-day mandate to supervise elections after dismissing the National Assembly and sacking prime minister Benazir Bhutto on disputed charges of corruption and misrule on November 5.
